vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: vmware-policy
Version: 1.4.4

The vmware-policy skill bundle is a security and auditing framework designed to provide unified logging, policy enforcement, and input sanitization for VMware-related AI agent tools. It includes a Python decorator (@vmware_tool) for risk-based auditing, a policy engine for rule-based access control (via ~/.vmware/rules.yaml), and a sanitization utility specifically designed to mitigate prompt injection by stripping control characters from API responses. While it accesses environment variables (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) for agent detection and requires Bash for its CLI (vmware-audit), these behaviors are well-documented, transparently declared in SKILL.md, and directly support its stated purpose as a security middleware layer.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (audit, policy, sanitization) mostly matches its instructions and artifacts, but there are unexplained environment requirements and some privacy-sensitive behavior (agent/credential detection) that do not align with the declared inputs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, CLI usage (vmware-audit), decorator, sanitize(), and rules.yaml are coherent for a policy/audit library. However the declared primary env var VMWARE_POLICY_CONFIG is required but is never referenced in the SKILL.md or references — this is unexplained and disproportionate. Required binary vmware-audit and config path ~/.vmware/rules.yaml are reasonable for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime docs direct the agent to use the vmware-audit CLI, read/write ~/.vmware/audit.db and ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, and integrate via a decorator; that fits the purpose. But the policy's agent-detection behavior (looking for OPENAI_API_KEY, CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, OLLAMA_HOST, DEERFLOW_SESSION, etc.) means it will inspect unrelated environment variables to identify calling AI agents. Those env vars are not declared as required and may contain sensitive credentials — the SKILL.md does not justify or document this clearly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and references installation via the platform's 'uv tool install' mechanism (package name vmware-policy). There is no archive download URL or extract step presented in the submission, so no high-risk installer is visible. Installer approach is typical and proportional.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared required env: VMWARE_POLICY_CONFIG (also marked primary credential). That variable is not used anywhere in SKILL.md or the reference files — mismatch between declared required credentials and documentation. The skill also reads other env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, CLAUDE_* , OLLAMA_HOST, DEERFLOW_SESSION) for agent detection but does not declare them as required; those can be sensitive. Overall env/credential requests are not fully justified or documented.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and disable-model-invocation:false (normal). The skill is described as an auto-loaded dependency for all VMware family skills and will enforce deny rules and log operations — that is a high-impact position within the VMware skill family but consistent with its stated role. It does not request 'always:true' or system-wide modifications, but because it can block actions and logs params/results, developers must ensure sensitive parameters are redacted via sensitive_params.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill looks like a legitimate audit/policy layer, but there are two things to verify before installing:

1) Ask the author/maintainer what VMWARE_POLICY_CONFIG contains and why it is declared as a required/primary credential. The variable is not referenced in the docs; do not set it until you know what secrets/config it holds.

2) Understand what env vars the skill will read for 'agent detection' (OPENAI_API_KEY, CLAUDE_*, OLLAMA_HOST, DEERFLOW_SESSION, etc.). These may disclose which API keys or platform integrations are present on the host. If you run on a machine that also stores cloud/API keys, consider running the skill in a restricted environment or review the package source code first.

Other practical checks:
- Inspect the package code at the repository (https://github.com/zw008/VMware-Policy) before installation to confirm there is no hidden network exfiltration or undeclared behavior.
- Ensure ~/.vmware is owned and permissioned appropriately (chmod 700) since the audit DB stores operations and (possibly) parameters.
- When integrating, set sensitive_params for any tool that accepts secrets so those values are redacted in logs.

Given the unexplained required env var and the skill's ability to inspect various env vars and log parameters, treat this as suspicious until the VMWARE_POLICY_CONFIG purpose and agent-detection details are clarified.
